transcript.text: Hi Sneha, good to meet you. I'd like to have a first conversation with you about this role. It should take about 15 minutes, and there'll be time for your questions at the end. What course or project at IIM Kozhikode has caught your attention recently?
transcript.why: This was a warm-up question to help you settle in. It isn't part of the feedback.

transcript.text: um hi sir nice to meet you too so actually one course that I found quite interesting is the marketing management basics one in term one because like we discussed a lot about consumer behavior and it felt very practical also um project wise I liked working on a group case for rural marketing but sorry I don’t remember all the details now
Thanks. Walk me through your background, up to how your first term at the MBA has gone.
transcript.why: I moved on after your response to begin with your academic and professional background.

transcript.text: um so basically I did my BSc in biotechnology from Christ University in Bangalore and during that time I was quite active with extracurriculars also like leading the cultural committee and all then after that I did two internships one in research at Biocon Biologics and another in retail marketing at Nature’s Basket and now I’ve just completed my first term at IIM Kozhikode where honestly it was a bit tough in the academic sense but I’m learning a lot and trying to catch up with the fast pace
Thanks, that gives me the outline of your path. You’ve moved from biotechnology into marketing. What’s pulling you toward marketing after your first term at IIM Kozhikode?
transcript.why: Your answer outlined your path from biotechnology through internships to your MBA, so I moved to what is drawing you toward marketing.

transcript.text: um actually sir I feel like marketing is more dynamic and people-oriented and I enjoyed that part more during my internships especially when we got to interact with customers also in classes I realized I like thinking about what makes consumers behave in certain ways instead of just lab research so I want to explore that more
Which specific moment during your Nature’s Basket or Biocon internship first made marketing feel like a direction you wanted to pursue?
transcript.why: Your answer explained what appeals to you about marketing, but not which specific experience first led you there. I asked for one concrete example to understand that link.

transcript.text: um so actually during my Nature’s Basket internship when I did the in-store sampling for the millet range I got to talk directly with a lot of customers and listen to their feedback and it was really interesting to see how just conversations or small changes can affect what people buy so that made me feel marketing is exciting and suits me better
Let’s look more closely at that Nature’s Basket work. I see you ran in-store sampling for an organic millet range. What were you trying to achieve?
transcript.why: Your answer connected your interest in marketing to a specific customer-facing experience during the Nature's Basket internship. I moved on to understand the work behind that experience.

transcript.text: um so mainly the goal was to increase awareness for that millet range and encourage more customers to actually try and buy it because before that those products were just sitting on the shelf and not moving much so in-store sampling was meant to get more people to taste and consider buying
Which part of the sampling activity did you personally decide or handle?
transcript.why: Your answer explained what the campaign was intended to achieve, but not which parts you personally handled. I asked about your specific role in running the sampling.

transcript.text: um so actually I got to plan how to approach customers like what to say during the sampling and I also kept track of who tried the samples and their feedback plus I suggested that we put up simple signs in Malayalam because many shoppers preferred that language and then I shared the feedback with my manager
How did you calculate the 18% conversion figure?
transcript.why: You described what you personally handled, but not how the 18% figure was produced. I asked how the conversion rate was defined and counted so the result could be understood clearly.

transcript.text: um so basically I counted how many people actually tasted the samples during the sampling days and then noted how many of them ended up buying the millet product immediately after that and then I divided the buyers by total samplers to get the percentage um sorry I don’t remember the exact numbers now
Understood. Let’s move to a different situation. Tell me about a time you disagreed with your team or took a stance.
transcript.why: Your answer explained how you calculated the percentage, but the exact counts behind it were not available. I’m moving on to hear about a different kind of situation.

transcript.text: um okay so during my cultural committee work in college there was once a disagreement about which external artists to invite for the fest like most of the team wanted to go for energetic bands but I felt a classical act would reach more of our audience so I shared my view and explained why but later we did a mix of both so it was a compromise
After explaining your view, what did you do first to move the discussion toward a decision?
transcript.why: You explained the position you took and the eventual compromise, so I asked what you did specifically to move the discussion forward.

transcript.text: um so after I explained I actually asked everyone to share their opinions and like why they preferred certain artists and I tried to listen to both sides and see if there was any common ground then I suggested maybe we can split the performance slots between both types so everyone feels included
Let’s turn to your leadership experience. What was the hardest part of leading the cultural committee’s annual fest?
transcript.why: Your answer explained your position and the steps you took to help the group reach a decision, so I moved to another leadership example.

transcript.text: um so actually the hardest part was managing the coordination between so many different teams like logistics, finance, promotions and even the volunteers because everyone was busy with their own college work also so getting everyone on the same page and making sure things happened on time was quite challenging for me
Which part of coordinating logistics, finance, promotions, and volunteers did you personally handle?
transcript.why: You described the coordination challenge across several teams, but not which parts you personally handled. I asked this to understand your contribution to keeping the event on track.

transcript.text: um so mainly I was involved in coordinating with the promotions and volunteer teams like setting up schedules for volunteers and discussing with the promotions lead how to spread the word on campus and on social media for logistics and finance I mostly just checked in on progress but didn’t handle the main planning directly
When you were setting volunteer schedules, what was the first thing you did to keep everyone aligned?
transcript.why: You clarified which coordination work was personally yours, so I asked how you carried it out. This checks the steps you took to keep the event moving.

transcript.text: um so the first thing I did was make a WhatsApp group with all the volunteers and then I put up the full event schedule and like assigned time slots for everyone based on their availability which I collected using a simple Google form so that everyone could see who is on duty when and we could avoid confusion
Let’s try a different marketing example. Tell me about another time you had to understand what customers wanted or improve how something was presented.
transcript.why: Your answer explained the steps you took to organize volunteers. We’re moving to a different marketing example to understand how you handled another practical situation.

transcript.text: um so during my Biocon internship even though it was more on the research side I did a small literature summary about cold-chain failures and I had to check with some staff about what kind of issues usually happen when insulin gets transported and why it matters for patients in South India so I tried to present those findings in a way that would be easy for my mentor and their team to use but um sorry I don’t have a very marketing-heavy example apart from that
What did your mentor or team do with the summary after you presented it?
transcript.why: Your example explained what you investigated and who you consulted, but not what happened afterward. I asked what changed because of the summary.

transcript.text: um so after I shared the summary my mentor actually said it was helpful for their ongoing project on improving the cold chain systems and I think they used some of the cases I found for their team discussions but honestly I don’t know a lot about what happened with it after that since my internship ended soon after
Thanks, Sneha. That’s everything from my side. What questions do you have for me?
transcript.why: You described how you gathered and presented information, along with what your mentor did with it afterward. That gave a concrete example of applying customer or stakeholder insight.

transcript.text: um thank you sir so I wanted to ask how does the company usually support new joiners who are transitioning from science backgrounds like is there some kind of structured training or mentorship also if I get selected what kind of roles or projects can a fresher expect in the first year that’s all I wanted to know I don’t have more questions

I’d rather not guess about the company’s specific training, mentorship structure, or first-year assignments. The hiring team can share those details, including how science backgrounds are supported. Is there anything else you’d like to know?
transcript.why: You asked about support for transitioning from science into marketing and the kind of work a fresher might do in the first year, so I responded to those questions directly.

transcript.text: um no sir that’s all right thank you for clarifying I don’t have any more questions right now thanks for your time
Thank you for your time, Sneha. That concludes the interview, and your feedback is ready.
transcript.why: You indicated that you had no further questions, so I closed the interview.

priorities.title: Make outcomes concrete
priorities.why: Specific results help an interviewer judge the value of your actions rather than only hearing what you intended.
priorities.action: When a follow-up asks what changed after your action, state the measured result or clearly label what you do not know.

priorities.title: Name your marketing direction
priorities.why: A specific target helps the interviewer understand why this role fits your move from biotechnology.
priorities.action: Prepare a short link between customer insight, marketing execution, and your biotechnology background.

priorities.title: Clarify your leadership scope
priorities.why: Clear ownership shows what you can be trusted to handle in a team setting.
priorities.action: Practise separating the areas you coordinated from the areas you only monitored.
